content.title: What time is Artemis launch today? Watch Artemis II launch in Northeast
content.text: April 1, 2026, 10:31 a.m. ETWhat time is the rocket launch today? Artemis II launch is ready for liftoff, and all eyes are on NASA's space launch this evening, with a crew of four astronauts set to take on an Artemis II mission around the moon and back. Can I watch Artemis 2 launch from the Northeast, and where can I livestream Artemis II liftoff today?Here's what to know about the Artemis II launch today, and if the rocket launch is visible in Washington DC, Virginia, Maryland, Delaware, Pennsylvania, New Jersey and across the Mid-Atlantic states.The launch window at the Kennedy Space Center near Cape Canaveral, Florida, opens at 6:24 p.m. ET, and you can watch Artemis II launch live through NASA live stream via NASA's YouTube page (livestreaming now), the NASA website or the NASA+ mobile app. USA TODAY's Florida Today Space Team will provide Artemis II moon launch live coverage ahead of liftoff. NASA has a two-hour window to attempt Artemis II liftoff — meaning Artemis 2 launch could be as late as 8:24 p.m. ET.Four astronauts are currently on-track to launch from Pad 39B atop NASA's Space Launch System (SLS) rocket, taking the Orion spacecraft on a 10-day test flight around the moon. Artemis II won't land on the moon; however, the space mission will mark humanity's deepest venture into space since the Apollo missions — and pick up where the 1972 Apollo 17 mission left off, the last time humans set foot on the moon.Today's space rocket launch will also tee up an upcoming Artemis III test flight in 2027, Artemis IV landing in 2028 and NASA's plan to set up a lunar base. If all goes as plan, the crew — commander Reid Wiseman, pilot Victor Glover, and mission specialists Christina Koch and Jeremy Hansen — will get a remarkable view from the far side of the moon and set a record for the farthest distance from Earth at 252,000 miles, surpassing the record set by Apollo 13.With the Florida weather forecast looking good for the space launch — NASA has strict weather guidelines to launch the SLS and Orion spacecraft — is it possible to see the rocket launch near me? Here's details on how to watch the Artemis II launch, time, livestream, rocket path, moon mission details and more as Artemis II fueling gets underway this morning ahead of liftoff.Is there a rocket launch today? Artemis II launchWill Artemis II launch today? Yes! The NASA Artemis II rocket launch today, April 1, from Kennedy Space Center in Cape Canaveral, Florida, is set to send four astronauts on a 10-day mission around the moon in a NASA-owned SLS rocket, testing the Orion spacecraft's life support systems for the first time with humans. If liftoff today goes as planned, the space mission could set the record for the farthest distance ever traveled from Earth, at 252,000 miles, surpassing the Apollo 13 mission.Today's Artemis 2 launch is a test for future missions to land astronauts on the moon in 2028. Artemis II will not land on the moon.What time is Artemis II launch today? Lift off for Artemis 2The 2-hour window for Artemis II launch time today, April 1, opens at 6:24 p.m. ET, meaning if the weather forecast is favorable, Artemis 2 liftoff could happen anytime between 6:24 p.m. ET to 8:24 p.m. ET. Artemis II launch live updates can be found on the NASA website here, with Florida Today, part of the USA TODAY Network, providing live coverage.How to watch Artemis 2 launch; Artemis II livestreamTo watch Artemis II launch today, you can head to the NASA YouTube page to catch the Artemis II livestream, or watch the rocket launch on NASA+ on your computer desktop, from the NASA website, or download NASA+ app on you iPhone or Samsung phone.Local TV channels CBS, ABC, NBC, and Fox News will broadcast the launch 2026. Have Amazon Prime Video or Peacock? You can also stream the rocket launch today on Prime, either through your TV or on your phone.The NASA live stream has been active since 7:45 a.m. ET today, with the latest mission updates showing Artemis II fueling underway as of 10 a.m. ET ahead of launch this evening.Watch Artemis II launch on Amazon Prime VideoCan I see space launch near me? Artemis II launch path, visibility mapCan I see Artemis II launch near me? If you are in Florida or Georgia, you have the best chance of seeing the space launch near you, but it's possible you may spot the rocket along the East Coast since the Artemis II launch path is headed east. If the weather is ideal, Artemis II could be visible in New Jersey, Pennsylvania, Virginia, Maryland, Ohio, West Virginia, Delaware, Washington DC and along the Mid-Atlantic states.The SpaceX Atlas V rocket — which lifted off from Cape Canaveral in Florida on March 1 — was spotted as far as North Jersey, and other NASA space launches have been seen from DC to NJ in years past. Keep an eye to the sky!Where is Artemis II going? Will Artemis II land on the moon?No, Artemis II will not land on the lunar surface, but the four Artemis II astronauts will fly around the moon for about 10 days. The mission is to test systems and equipment, laying the groundwork for future missions to land on the moon.Is Artemis 2 launch on schedule? NASA live streamYes, Artemis II launch is on schedule as of 10 a.m. ET today, April 1, with fueling underway and the four astronauts preparing to launch, per the NASA live stream.According to NASA, the crew woke up at 9:25 a.m. ET today, had a meal, will attend a weather briefing and then head to the "suit up room" to put on their orange Orion Crew Survival System suits around 12:50 p.m. ET. They will depart for Pad 39B launch pad about 4 hours, 40 minutes before launch — although this could be a moving target pending any propellant loading delays.It takes about 40 minutes for the astronauts to get strapped into their seats. The last people to see the astronauts? A five-person crew known as the "closeout crew," will perform leak checks on Orion's hatches before launch.Lori Comstock is a New Jersey-based news reporter covering trending news with USA TODAY Network's Mid-Atlantic Connect Team. She covers health and other news in the Northeast, including New Jersey, Pennsylvania, Delaware, Washington DC, Maryland, and Virginia. Reach her at LComstock@usatodayco.com.
